name: Austin Rogers

items.text: At a May 2026 Republican primary debate, rival Jim Norton questioned whether Florida's 2nd District was really home for Rogers. Rogers pushed back. He moved back from Virginia, where he lived while his wife trained as a doctor.
items.why: This is a residency dispute bearing on commitment to the area (criterion 1), but it is a rival's challenge with no official finding against Rogers.

for_review: I could not read the full text of the key pages. The WFSU debate page returned only navigation and metadata. The flvoicenews attack-ad article and the Florida Politics debate and residency articles would not open. Item 1 and item 2 text rests on the item descriptions plus search-result excerpts from Florida Politics (Sept. 14, 2026) and flvoicenews. Please read those pages before publishing. Check these points. (1) Rogers's actual Florida voter registration date, which the ad puts at March 17, 2026. A Florida Politics correction says he first pre-registered in 2008 and is now registered at a different address. (2) What Florida Politics reported on Sept. 14, 2026. It said he listed a rental home when he re-registered and still owned a D.C.-area home, and his campaign said he and his family live in the district. (3) Which 'former employer' the ad means, and what the China business was. His known past employer is Sen. Rick Scott's office, where he was general counsel, so the ad may mean a private firm. I found nothing on this. Rogers won the Nov. 3, 2026 general election. The owner-site search found nothing substantive on Rogers. One alexjoneslive.com reader comment called him pro-Israel, but it is anonymous and is not evidence. I added no items of my own. I found no court or official finding against Rogers, and I used no searches on his finances or donors. AIPAC-related matters are counted separately.
